interval_scope: IID binomial working model conditional on the released sample; sampling/selection bias is excluded.

frequentist.standard_error_method: Conventional unpooled Bernoulli plug-in Wald standard error.
frequentist.hc2_interpretation: HC2 from Y ~ 1 + T equals s1^2/n1 + s0^2/n0; use this SE when comparing with Lin adjustment.
frequentist.mde_assumptions: Two-sided alpha=0.05, target power=0.80, local normal approximation at the released control rate.

jeffreys.loss_units: Outcome probability per user; no monetary cost or value is assumed.

uniform.loss_units: Outcome probability per user; no monetary cost or value is assumed.

limitations: Nonuniform sub-sampling prevents recovering Criteo's original incrementality level; effects describe the released sample.
All intervals are unadjusted for multiple outcomes; visit is primary and conversion is exploratory.
Rare conversion alone does not imply inadequate power; sample size, effect size and the decision threshold also matter.
No independent historical data were available for an informative prior.

iv_exploratory.interpretation: The Wald ratio describes this released sample under the listed IV assumptions; it does not estimate Criteo's actual advertising effect. Under one-sided noncompliance, all observed exposed users are compliers. With random assignment, they are representative of the complier population, so the CACE also equals the average effect of exposure on the exposed (ATT), subject to the assumptions and sampling caveat above.
required_assumptions: Random assignment within the released sample, with positivity.
Exclusion: assignment affects the outcome only through exposure.
Relevance: treatment assignment increases exposure probability.
One-sided noncompliance: no control user is exposed.
SUTVA: no interference between users and a single version of exposure.

visit.naive_comparison_interpretation: A descriptive association subject to exposure selection bias.

conversion.naive_comparison_interpretation: A descriptive association subject to exposure selection bias.

warnings: Covariate balance cannot prove randomization, exclusion, or valid IV identification.
The estimate inherits any error in recorded exposure and the public-data sampling caveat.
